ev.q: HIV Outbreak During the COVID-19 Pandemic Among Persons Who Inject Drugs — Kanawha County, West Virginia, 2019–2021
HIV Outbreak During the COVID-19 Pandemic Among Persons Who Inject Drugs
An HIV outbreak case was defined as a confirmed HIV diagnosis on or after January 1, 2019 in a PWID living in Kanawha County
in May 2021 requested CDC assistance with an HIV outbreak investigation
Recommendations based on investigation findings and HIV surveillance data are guiding response activities.
Investigators conducted qualitative interviews with 26 PWID and 45 community partners
abstracted medical records for 496 health care encounters beginning 1 year before HIV diagnosis through June 18, 2021

equity.level_reason: Sex, age, race/ethnicity and unstable housing appear only as descriptors of the case series; no group-specific results by an SPD are reported. Structural factors (SSP closures, legislation, stigma) explain the outbreak among PWID, a behavior-defined population.

level_alternative.reason: Unstable housing could be read as an individual risk-factor descriptor of cases, leaving only age and sex descriptors.

determinants_of_health.v: limited access to sterile syringes after SSP closures; legislation restricting SSPs; stigma and discrimination in health care settings

ev.q: PWID reported reusing or sharing syringes, mainly because of limited access to sterile syringes after SSP closures.
PWID expressed medical mistrust because of experiences of stigma and discrimination in health care settings.
low SSP access because of some community opposition to evidence-based SSPs and new legislation restricting SSPs

equity.equity_measurement: Case composition only (sex, age, race, unstable housing); no SPD groups compared; PWID is a behavior-defined population.

notes: data_focus is yes because diagnosis counts are compared across periods (pre-2019 vs 2019), though most content is descriptive. Molecular clustering is a linkage classification, not a procedure. Determinants are recorded as explanations of the PWID outbreak, though PWID is not a listed SPD.
view_issues: Text reports 54 (52%) of 85 patients male; 54/85 is 64%, so the count or the percentage is wrong.
